title: Learning Multiscale Dynamics of Nanoparticle Self-Assembly
authors: Shuaifeng Li, Puquan Pan, Jonas Hallstrom, Nicholas Kotov, Paul Bogdan, Qian Chen, Xiaoming Mao
abstract: Nanoparticle self-assembly offers a powerful route to programmable functional materials, but its dynamics remain difficult to understand because they arise from multiscale, many-body, and environment-dependent interactions. Liquid-phase transmission electron microscopy (LPTEM) enables real-time observation of these dynamics, yet extracting the underlying physical laws from highly stochastic trajectories remains a significant challenge. Here we develop a physics-informed, time-varying autoregressive framework that learns multiscale self-assembly dynamics directly from LPTEM videos. Continuous Eulerian fields with local density and orientational order are coarse-grained from individual video frames and evolved by a sparse, nearest-neighbor operator optimized over a constrained matrix manifold. This interpretable approach captures long-time large scale phase transitions by tracking operator volatility over time, and short-timescale local evolution and transport rules. Crucially, we extract the underlying partial differential equations, where expected symmetries naturally emerge, enabling the direct inference of fundamental coefficients. Our framework provides a robust, computationally efficient tool for discovering hidden physical mechanisms from observational data, opening a path toward the predictive design of self-assembled nanostructures.
summary: This work introduces a novel physics-informed machine learning framework to decipher the complex dynamics of nanoparticle self-assembly directly from LPTEM videos. By modeling the evolution of coarse-grained fields using a time-varying autoregressive operator, the authors achieve high interpretability. This allows for the extraction of underlying partial differential equations, providing a predictive tool for designing functional nanostructures.
main_problem: Understanding the complex, multiscale, and environment-dependent dynamics of nanoparticle self-assembly from stochastic, real-time experimental observations.
main_result: The framework successfully learns dynamics capturing both long-time phase transitions and short-timescale local evolution, extracting underlying Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) consistent with physical symmetries.
method: A physics-informed, time-varying autoregressive framework is developed to model the evolution of coarse-grained Eulerian fields ($ho, Q$) using a sparse, nearest-neighbor operator optimized on a matrix manifold.
model_or_system: The system is nanoparticle self-assembly, observed via Liquid-phase transmission electron microscopy (LPTEM). The state is modeled by coupled continuous fields: local density ($ho$) and orientational order parameters ($Q_1, Q_2$).
key_observables: Operator volatility (for phase transitions), cumulative propagator spectral decomposition, and extracted PDE coefficients.
important_parameters: Time-varying operator $A_t$, regularization parameters ($\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \lambda_3$), and the nearest-neighbor interaction range.
main_assumptions: The dynamics can be linearly advanced by a time-varying operator $A_t$, and the dominant interactions are short-ranged (nearest-neighbor).
figures_summary: Figures show raw particle positions alongside coarse-grained Eulerian fields ($ho, Q_1, Q_2$) at various times, illustrating the structure of the learned nearest-neighbor operator $A_t$.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the challenge of multiscale dynamics, details the TVAR framework with manifold optimization, analyzes dynamics using operator volatility and propagator decomposition, and concludes by extracting interpretable PDEs.
why_interesting: The method provides a powerful, data-driven bridge between noisy, high-dimensional experimental trajectories and continuum field theories, which is highly relevant for modeling complex many-body dynamics in non-equilibrium systems.
